All 32,768 edge colorings of the complete six-vertex graph satisfy the stated Ramsey triangle conclusion. Simple undirected graphs on two through six vertices were checked for repeated degree. General proofs remain necessary beyond those finite ranges.

All 33 preceding chapter bodies and their 1,917 question entries are preserved; only the inclusion-exclusion header records the user's explicit approval. Six written courses were genuinely reviewed, with five selected primary courses from four universities and Cornell as a complementary text.

Restart, previous/next, seek, speed, play/pause and real moving elements were exercised. Authentic archive boundary

MSc CS 1405 Q116 and PhD CS 1404 Q25 were checked visually against their original physical PDF pages. The former is a newly verified finite-search bridge; the latter is a parity-counting revisit. Original printed options and independently derived answers remain identifiable. No external official answer-key verification is claimed.

Scientific qualifications

Sharpness requires a realizable avoiding example; a sufficient grid bound is not a universal packing optimum. One-lie transcript packing and the deck-state inequality are necessary information bounds unless an explicit strategy is proved. The monotone theorem's strict form requires distinct values. Prime two is handled separately in square-image counting. Positivity and modular invertibility are checked before subset cancellation. Finite tests supplement these general written proofs and do not guarantee every unseen examination question.
